_README: Measured kernel cycles, consumed by loop/llama_project.py.
Entries with `cycles: null` are PLACEHOLDERS until someone fills them in
from a real Verilator run (the SoC does ~1.8k cycles/s, so only single
kernels are measurable; the whole model is projected, never simulated).
Fields:
kernel         one of the kernel types in loop/llama_model.py
shape          the shape that was actually measured (documentation)
work_metric    'macs' or 'elems' - which quantity cycles scale with
work_measured  value of that metric at the measured shape
cycles         total cycles for one call at that shape (null = not measured)
overhead_cycles  fixed per-call cost (setup, config, fences) subtracted
before linear extrapolation and re-added per call
device         'gemmini' or 'saturn' - which unit ran it
source         where the number came from
Scaling rule applied by llama_project.py:
cycles(target) = calls*overhead + (cycles - overhead) * work_target/work_measured
Entries with cycles == null fall back to roofline x --fallback-factor and
are flagged 'est' in the output tables.
HOW TO SWITCH decode GEMV BETWEEN SATURN AND GEMMINI
project() looks up `<kernel>_<unit>` first when `--device kernel=unit` is
given on the CLI (e.g. `--device int8_gemv=gemmini` -> `int8_gemv_gemmini`),
and falls back to the bare `<kernel>` entry otherwise. An entry's own
`device` field is only used when the CLI did NOT pin that kernel.
The two candidate numbers for the SAME decode GEMV shape (M=512, K=2048,
1,048,576 MACs, 1 MiB of weights) are:
saturn  621724 cycles  (1.69 B/cycle of weights)  <- naive RVV baseline
gemmini 150339 cycles  (6.97 B/cycle of weights)  <- 4.1x faster
So: no --device -> saturn (bare entries); `--device int8_gemv=gemmini
--device lm_head_gemv=gemmini` -> the *_gemmini entries.
WHY MAC-LINEAR SCALING IS OK FOR A DECODE GEMV
At N=1 a GEMV does exactly one MAC per weight byte, so scaling by MACs is
scaling by weight traffic - which is what actually costs cycles here. Do
NOT extrapolate the N=64 `int8_gemm` measurement down to decode: at N=64
the weight mvin is amortized over 64 rows of work, at N=1 over one. That
extrapolation predicted ~9.01M cycles/token, below the 78M memory roofline
for 1.24 GB of weights, i.e. impossible. The measured N=1 rate of
6.97 B/cycle gives ~178M cycles/token instead.
THE SEVEN NON-GEMM OPERATORS (measured 2026-09-05, Saturn)
rmsnorm, rope, attn_scores, softmax, attn_pv, silu_mul and add are now
real Verilator numbers from the `llama-<op>` benchmarks in
repos/saturn/benchmarks/, registered in loop/kernels.py and run with
`loop.py --kernel llama-<op> --baseline-only --config
GENV256D128GemminiShuttleConfig`. All seven are PRISTINE naive RVV 1.0
baselines (LMUL=1, no unrolling, no reuse) - they were written to be
MEASURED, not optimized, because together they are ~1% of decode cycles.
Every one of them has 2.5x-60x of headroom to its own roofline; see the
`notes` on each Kernel entry in loop/kernels.py for where it is.
dtype: fp32 activations throughout, matching ModelSpec.acc_bytes = 4.
attn_scores and attn_pv are now costed from the **int8 KV cache**
variants (`llama-attn-scores-q8kv`, `llama-attn-pv-q8kv`), which match
ModelSpec's kv_bytes = 1: K/V stored int8 with one fp32 dequant scale
per KV row, q and P still fp32. The fp32-cache measurements of the
identical shape are kept under each entry's additional_measurements.
SURPRISE, AND IT IS THE INTERESTING RESULT HERE: the int8 cache is
SLOWER, not faster - 68,571 vs 60,147 for attn_scores (1.14x) and
62,541 vs 44,765 for attn_pv (1.40x). Quartering the cache took the
memory floor from 8,192 to 2,304 cycles, but because q/P stay fp32
every cached byte must be widened int8 -> int32 -> fp32 before it can
be multiplied: two extra 32-bit-destination ops per element, which
raises the ARITHMETIC floor from 8,192 to 24,576. The kernel goes from
perfectly balanced to compute-bound by 10x. On this SoC, at this shape,
quantising only the cache is a losing trade.
That prediction was then TESTED. `llama-attn-scores-int8` and
`llama-attn-pv-int8` quantise the activation side as well (int8 q with a
per-vector scale; int8 probabilities with V's per-row scales folded in,
since a cross-row reduction cannot carry a per-row scale), accumulate in
int32 with vwmul + vwadd.wv, and do exactly one fp32 multiply per output.
Three measurements of the identical 512x64 shape, all equally naive:
variant   cache        activation   attn_scores   attn_pv
int8      int8  32KiB  int8              51,280    22,856
So quantising the cache ALONE loses (1.14x / 1.40x slower than fp32) and
quantising BOTH sides wins (1.17x / 1.96x faster than fp32, and 1.34x /
2.74x faster than cache-only). The arithmetic floors say why:
variant   memory floor   arithmetic floor   binding
fp32             8,192              8,192   balanced
q8kv             2,304             24,576   compute, 10x
int8             2,300              8,192   compute, ~3.6x
int8 activations delete the per-element vsext+vfcvt, putting the
arithmetic floor back where fp32's was while keeping a quarter of the
traffic - the only one of the three with slack on BOTH resources.
Accuracy is not the obstacle: measured relative L2 error against a true
fp32 reference is 1.7e-3 (scores) and 2.9e-3 (pv), 10-17x inside the
3e-2 gate. Each of those kernels also carries an EXACT int32 self-check,
so quantisation tolerance never hides a kernel bug.
The primary cost basis above is still the q8kv (int8 cache, fp32
activation) entry, deliberately: moving the model to full int8 attention
changes the attention CONTRACT (softmax must emit int8 probabilities and
q_proj must emit an int8 query), which is a model decision and not a
kernel optimization. The full-int8 numbers are recorded under each
entry's additional_measurements so the switch can be costed the moment
it is taken: it would move decode from 261.68M to 232.51M cycles/token
(3.82 -> 4.30 tokens/s) and prefill from 16.42M to 14.57M (60.9 -> 68.6).
Both are measured for ONE query head (32,768 MACs); MAC-linear scaling
multiplies them by the 32 heads x 16 layers the profile asks for.
`rope` is ONE measurement covering both rope calls of a layer (rope_q
2048 elems + rope_k 512 elems = 2560); elems-linear scaling splits it.
STILL ESTIMATED (cycles == null -> roofline x --fallback-factor):
embedding     a 2048-byte row gather out of the 128256x2048 table
lm_head_gemm  the prefill output projection (same shape as lm_head_gemv)
In prefill the seven measurements above are extrapolated from their decode
shapes by elems/macs, which is right for the elementwise ops (N tokens is
N times the elements) but optimistic for attn_scores/attn_pv, where the
causal N(N+1)/2 shape is a different kernel, not a longer one.

loop baseline llama-q8-gemv-gemmini-n16 2026-09-05. Same 1 MiB of weights as the N=1 point: 16x the MACs for 12% more cycles (6.23 B/cycle vs 6.97), which is what 'weight-bandwidth bound' looks like. Batching decode to N=16 is nearly free; past 16 use the int8_gemm measurement. Documentation only - MeasuredDB.load keys one Measurement per kernel name.

notes: PRE-ROUND1 measured rates against the same 1 MiB of weights:
N=1  150339 cycles -> 6.97 B/cycle (44% of the 16 B/cycle DMA peak),
The array is ~97% idle at N=1 and that is correct: 15 of every 16 rows
fed through the 16x16 array are zero padding, and the weights arrive far
slower than the array can eat them. Decode on this SoC is a memory
-> 7.91 B/cycle (49% of DMA peak). Still DMA-bound; roofline 65536 unchanged.
